standfirst: What this module calls, what it was built from, and where it stops. Every number on this page comes from a measurement file in the build directory.
lede01: A second module exists for one reason: these genomes carry the minor-glycoprotein cassette twice.
p01: The module covers Simarterivirinae, the simian arteriviruses — simian haemorrhagic fever virus and its relatives in African and Asian primates. They are split from the rest of Arteriviridae on genome organisation, not phylogeny, and the organisation in question is a duplicated cassette: where every other arterivirus carries one set of minor envelope glycoproteins, these carry two (PMID 25036340).

That gives 14 features. Nine are the ordinary arterivirus set — ORF1A, GP2, E, GP3, GP4, ORF5A, GP5, M, N — plus ORF1AB from the −1 ribosomal frameshift. The remaining four are the duplicate copies: EP, GP2P, GP3P and GP4P.

The four carry the annotation “Uncharacterized lineage-specific protein” and an unnumbered family symbol, because no publication assigns them a function distinct from their non-duplicated partners. That is the honest name, and it is also the rule: a paralogue with no literature function is not given one here.
lede02: Almost nothing in this module could be binned from the deposited annotation string.
p02: Of 79 distinct annotation strings over 284 occurrences, exactly one controlled target can be reached by name: ORF1A, from polyprotein, 1a replicase and their variants. 72 strings remain unbound. The source calls both cassette copies minor glycoprotein — 174 times in Etaarterivirus and 156 in Zetaarterivirus — and a name that cannot distinguish a protein from its own paralogue cannot bin either one.

So the thirteen structural features were separated by position in the cassette, and each orthogroup got its own PSSM. Position curates; sequence calls. The collections are near-uniform in size as a result — GP2, GP2P, GP3P, GP4P, GP5, M and N all at 171, GP3 166, GP4 168, E 169, ORF5A 165 — because each is one member per genome rather than whatever the submitters happened to name.
EP is the exception at 23 members: the duplicated E is present in a subset of the lineages, and it is not padded out to match the others.
lede03: One floor for almost everything, because the collections are one deposit per genome.
p03: Every structural feature carries a 30-bit floor at 0.65 coverage; ORF5A takes 25 and ORF1A 60. ORF1AB carries none, because it is a transcript edit built from the frameshift reference rather than called by a profile.

Nine features carry copy_num — E, GP2, GP3, GP4, GP5, M, N, ORF1A, ORF5A. The four paralogues do not, and neither does ORF1AB: an uncharacterized lineage-specific protein is exactly what must never be made essential, since every lineage lacking it would be flagged as defective.
lede04: Routing is a BLASTn of the query against the reference contigs.
p04: All 24 exemplars route and none fail to route. The module ships 11 reference contigs and the panel draws on every one. Eleven references for a subfamily of 54 genomes is generous, and deliberately so: the duplicated cassette is what defines the module, and a genome routed to the wrong module cannot have its paralogues separated at all.
Four of the eleven reference genomes sit in the panel, at 100% identity over their full length. The panel is therefore not held out, and the held-out figure is given below.
lede05: Calling is measured on the exemplars, feature by feature.
p05: Both copies of the cassette are called on essentially every genome, which is the one thing this module exists to do: GP2 25, GP2' 24, GP3 23, GP3' 24, GP4 24, GP4' 25, against 24 exemplars. The duplicated copies are not called more weakly than the originals — position curated the collections, and the profiles built from them separate the paralogues on sequence.
The rest of the set runs with them: ORF1A 24, GP5 24, M 24, N 24, E 24, ORF5A 24, and ORF1AB 23 from the −1 frameshift.

E' is called once, and that is the feature behaving correctly. The duplicated E is present in a subset of the lineages — its collection holds 23 members against 171 for the others — so a feature called on one exemplar is a feature called on the exemplar that has it. It carries no copy_num for exactly this reason.
lede06: The panel is scored on the annotator's own quality model.
p06: 20 of 24 genomes score Good, 4 Poor, with one “too short” and one “too long” flag over 290 calls.

With the four reference genomes removed: 20 held-out genomes, 17 Good, 3 Poor. The ratio barely moves, which is what a small, uniform panel should do — there is no divergent tail here for the references to be drawn from, because the subfamily is the tail.
lede07: The limits, each measured rather than supposed.
p07: Three genomes of 54 collapse part of the cassette onto one ORF, and the cause is downstream of the profile match rather than in it — the trace puts each feature in the right place, and the scan to a start and a stop then lands overlapping ORFs on the same coordinates. Recorded in detail below, and deliberately not patched.

The four paralogues are named “Uncharacterized lineage-specific protein” and that will not improve without new literature. No publication assigns GP2', GP3', GP4' or E' a function distinct from their partners. The module declines to invent one, and declines to make them essential.

The panel is 24 genomes. Every percentage on this page is over a set that small, and a single genome is four percentage points. The subfamily has 54 genomes in BV-BRC and 19 complete ones; no amount of care in the build makes that a large sample.
verdict07: Use this module on complete simian arterivirus genomes, and use it rather than the Arteriviridae module whenever the cassette is duplicated — that is the whole reason it exists. The nine features carrying copy_num are called in every complete genome routed here, with no exceptions. The four paralogues are called at the same rate as their partners but carry no copy_num, because a protein with no published function must never be the thing that marks a genome defective.
lede08: What the build turned up that was not expected.
p08: Three genomes of 54 collapse part of the cassette onto one ORF. In 2682610.4 (NC_048209) the layout is otherwise exactly right — GP2P 10806, GP3P 11354, GP4P 11878, GP2 12423, GP5 13732 — and the annotator's own trace puts GP3 at 12884-13210 and GP4 at 13229-13693, both correct. The collision happens after the profile match: ORF3 and ORF4 overlap in this family, and both features scan out to a start and a stop, so all three land on the same 271 aa ORF. 1885929.21 and .22 do the same with GP2 and GP2P. Recorded rather than patched.

Three nested calls are architecture, not defects. E inside GP2 (100% of calls), ORF1A inside ORF1AB (98%) and ORF5A inside GP5 (46%) are overlapping reading frames — ORF2b inside ORF2a, ORF5a inside ORF5. The default advice for a nested call is to raise the floor or drop the feature; here that would be exactly wrong, and the low similarity between the pairs (E vs GP2: 41% identity over 27% coverage, 19 bits) confirms they are different proteins sharing genome space.
lede09: What collapsing the vocabulary actually bought.
p09: The source uses 79 distinct product strings across the subfamily. 7 of them bind, all to the single controlled target ORF1A, over 284 occurrences. 72 bind to nothing.

The string-collapse page reports that as 79× (all distinct strings against one controlled target) and the tile here as 7.0× (bound strings against the same target). Here the two differ by the whole unbound set, which is the finding rather than an artefact of the arithmetic.

It is a measurement of the source, not of this module: the deposited vocabulary decides almost nothing, because the source calls both copies of the cassette minor glycoprotein — 174 times in Etaarterivirus and 156 in Zetaarterivirus — and a name that cannot tell a protein from its own paralogue cannot bin either one. The whole cassette was resolved by position.
